hub.title: Translate Emails in Apple Mail on Mac | Mailkin
hub.description: Apple Mail can't translate whole emails by itself. Mailkin adds automatic, on-device translation to Mail on your Mac in 25 languages.
hub.h1: Translate emails in Apple Mail on your Mac
hub.answer: Apple Mail on the Mac can't translate an email by itself: you can only select some text and choose Translate, one piece at a time. Mailkin adds automatic translation to Mail. Emails in other languages appear in your language as soon as you open them, translated on your Mac.
hub.builtinText: Not automatically. macOS has a Translate command: select text in an email, Control-click it and choose Translate. A small window shows the translation of that selection. You repeat it for every email, the email itself stays in the original language, and the formatting isn't kept.
hub.stepsTitle: How to translate every email automatically
steps: Download Mailkin and open it.
Choose the language you want to read email in, for example English.
Pick the languages you get email in. macOS downloads each one once from Apple.
In Mail, open Mail › Settings › Extensions and turn on Mailkin.
Open an email in one of your languages. It appears translated, with a banner saying which language it was in.
hub.stepsNote: Setup takes about two minutes. The Check Setup button in Mailkin confirms each step and can open a test email.
hub.lookTitle: What a translated email looks like
hub.lookText: The translation replaces the text in the message view and keeps the email's layout, links and images. A banner at the top says which language the email was in. Click Options on the banner to show the original, correct the detected language, or choose to always or never translate this email or this sender.
hub.privateTitle: Private: emails never leave your Mac
hub.privateText: Mailkin uses Apple's on-device translation, the same engine as the Translate app. No email text is sent to Mailkin, Apple or anyone else, and there is no account. Mailkin changes only what Mail shows: the emails in your mailbox stay exactly as they arrived. Signed emails are left untouched.
hub.accountsTitle: Works with every account in Mail
hub.accountsText: Mailkin works inside Mail, so it translates email from any account you've added there: iCloud, Gmail, Outlook and Exchange, Yahoo, or any other IMAP account.

sections:
Download Mailkin, open the disk image and drag Mailkin to Applications. Then open Mailkin and follow the setup. It takes about two minutes:

  1. Choose the language you want emails translated into.
  2. Pick the languages you get email in. macOS downloads each one once from Apple.
  3. In Mail, open Mail › Settings › Extensions and turn on Mailkin.

• Check its language is on. Mailkin only translates the languages switched on in its Languages tab, and only once they're downloaded.
  • Very long emails, over 20,000 characters like big newsletters, aren't translated automatically. Click Options on the email's banner, then Translate This Email.
  • Wrong language detected? Choose the right one under Language in the same Options.
  • Run Check Setup. Open Mailkin and click the stethoscope button at the top right. It checks each step and can open a test email in Mail to confirm translation works.
Click Options on the banner above a translated email, then Show Original. You can also set an email or a sender to Always translate or Don't translate.
Mailkin uses Apple's built-in translation, which supports 25 languages. See the full list of languages.

Your first 30 translated emails are free. After that, the one-time purchase Mailkin Translator Lifetime unlocks unlimited translation, with no subscription. Emails translated before stay translated. See Pricing.

• Unlocking: open Mailkin, click Unlock, paste the license key from your purchase email and click Activate. Paste the whole key, starting with MK1-.
  • Another Mac: enter the same key on every Mac you personally use.
  • Lost your key? Email us from the address you bought with and we'll send it again.
  • Refunds within 14 days: see the Refund Policy.

Bought it on another Mac, or through Family Sharing? Open Mailkin, click Unlock, then Restore Purchases.

For refunds, use reportaproblem.apple.com, since Apple handles App Store payments.
Turn off Mailkin in Mail › Settings › Extensions, then move Mailkin to the Trash. Your emails are not affected: Mailkin never changes the emails in your mailbox.

faq.title: Mailkin FAQ: Translating Email in Apple Mail
faq.description: Answers about Mailkin, the Mac app that translates emails in Apple Mail: privacy, languages, offline use, accounts, pricing and requirements.
items: What is Mailkin?
Mailkin is a Mac app that adds automatic translation to Apple Mail. When you open an email in another language, Mailkin shows it in your language, in place, with the original one click away.
Can Apple Mail translate emails by itself?

Only piece by piece. In Mail on the Mac you can select text, Control-click it and choose Translate, which shows a translation of the selection in a small window. Mailkin translates the whole email automatically when you open it, keeping its formatting.
Are my emails sent anywhere to be translated?
No. Mailkin uses Apple's built-in translation, which runs on your Mac. Your emails are not sent to Mailkin, Apple or any translation service, and there is no account.
Which languages does Mailkin translate?

25 languages: Arabic, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian and Vietnamese. See all languages.
Does it work offline?
Yes. macOS downloads each language you pick once from Apple. After that, translation works without an internet connection.
Does Mailkin change the emails in my mailbox?
No. It changes only what Mail displays. The emails stay exactly as they arrived, and Show Original brings the original text back.
Does it work with Gmail, Outlook or iCloud?
Yes, as long as you read that account in Apple Mail on your Mac. Mailkin translates email from any account added to Mail.
Does Mailkin translate emails I write or reply to?
Not yet. Mailkin translates the emails you receive.
Can I stop translating some emails or senders?
Yes. Use Options on an email's banner to always or never translate that email or sender, and choose per language whether Mailkin translates automatically, only when you ask, or never.
How much does Mailkin cost?
Your first 30 translated emails are free. After that, a one-time purchase of €14.99 / US$14.99 unlocks unlimited translation. There is no subscription. See Pricing.
What do I need to use it?
A Mac with macOS 26 or later and Apple Mail. Mailkin doesn't run on iPhone or iPad.
Where can I get Mailkin?
Download it from mailkin.app. It is coming soon to the Mac App Store.
How do I get a refund?
Purchases from mailkin.app can be refunded in full within 14 days; see the Refund Policy. App Store purchases are refunded by Apple.
